big_idea: We RECORD steps with arrows and pictures so anyone can follow.
learning_intention: We are learning to record steps with pictures.
student_learning_goal: I can record steps with pictures.
success_criteria: I can DRAW arrows for steps.
I can FOLLOW a picture code.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Bot the Robot — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Bot the Robot: To MOVE me, you need a CODE. Like a recipe — pictures of each step! Bot opens: 'WRITE the arrows, BOT will GO!' Day 1 we MOVED, Day 2 we FOUND, today we WRITE.
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Bot the Robot puppet. 'Coder friends — yesterday I MOVED with words. But what if my friend isn't here? I need to RECORD my code!'

Define. 'CODE = step-by-step instructions, recorded with arrows or pictures.'

Demo. Place Bot at corner A on mat with apple at B3. 'I want Bot to reach the apple. My code:'

Draw on board:
→ → ↑ ↑
(2 right, 2 up)

'Bot says — anyone can follow this code!'

Now show how recipes work. 'Same idea. Pancake recipe: 1) Mix flour. 2) Add milk. 3) Pour. 4) Cook. STEP BY STEP!'

Demo a 4-step code:
1. → (forward)
2. → (forward)
3. ↑ (turn up/right) — actually let's say: → (forward), → (forward), ⬆ (forward up), ⬆ (forward up).

Class reads code together. 'Forward, forward, up, up!'

'Bot says — codes are READ left to right!'

Now each pair gets a Code Strip + Arrow Cards. They place an apple, plan a route, and RECORD the code on the strip.

'Bot says — drawing code is FUN! It's like a treasure map.'

steps.instruction: Hand out Code Strips. Pairs place an apple on the mat.
Plan and record a 4-step code to reach apple.
Trade with another pair. Read their code and check.
Help with arrow direction (always read left-to-right).

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk the route while recording. NO-MATERIALS VERSION: children walk the 4 steps on a real floor grid; body becomes the code.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: draws; orders; reads; follows; consistency.

discussion_prompts: How do you READ a code?
How is code like a recipe?
consolidation.exit_routine: Bot's coding refrain — 'WRITE the arrows, BOT will GO!' (3x). Each child shows one code sequence + Bot's destination.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child draws arrows in WRONG ORDER — repairing the order trap at Kindergarten
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On writing pictograph code, the K trap is sequencing fragility (Bers 2018; Clements & Sarama 2014 on early CT): child orders arrows but skips steps mid-sequence. Without sequencing fluency, Lesson 4 debugging cannot ground.

Yesterday Lesson 1 moved Bot, Lesson 2 found Bot's position. Today: write the code with arrows. Lesson 4 debugs; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Code activity. Child draws → ↑ → → but wants Bot to go ↑ → → →.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Bot asks — what's STEP ONE?'

Probe. 'First step in code is FIRST arrow on left. Read left-to-right!'

Generalise. 'Bot says — order matters in CODE. STEP 1 first, then STEP 2.'

If still random: number the steps. '1, 2, 3, 4 — in order.'
common_misconceptions: Order doesn't matter. (Repair: order is critical.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child sequences but skips a step: drill 'every step gets ONE arrow'; child re-counts arrows vs squares moved.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child writes sequence but wrong order: drill 'first action is the FIRST arrow'.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child can sequence but can't articulate: force 'My code is ___ ___ ___; Bot will go to ___.'

parts_outline.task: Read 3 codes; circle the one that reaches the apple.
Draw a 4-step code on a Code Strip.
